title: Microsoft Purview: higher auto-labeling limits for SharePoint sites and simulation, plus new reporting
summary: Hold for a correction to the reporting instructions: the daily trend chart is on the full Overview page, not in the policy details panel or its Insights tab. The rollout, limits, licensing background and listed controls are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The general availability target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only listed cloud, with GCC, GCC High and DoD not listed.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The listed platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The listed release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: title; front matter: products, roadmapModified; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: This Microsoft Purview roadmap item concerns auto-labeling scalability, policy management and reporting enhancements.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Purview: Auto-labeling scalability, policy management, and reporting enhancements"; "modified": "2026-11-11T00:52:46"

claims.claim: The notice increases simulation capacity from 4 million to 20 million items.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling simulation capacity will increase from 4 million items to 20 million items.

claims.claim: The notice permits selecting up to 1,000 individual SharePoint sites when configuring policies.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to select up to 1,000 individual SharePoint sites when configuring policies.

claims.claim: The notice raises adaptive scope support to 50,000 SharePoint sites per policy.
claims.quote: Adaptive scopes will support up to 50,000 SharePoint sites per policy.

claims.claim: The notice adds SiteTemplate filtering for SharePoint sites during policy configuration.
claims.quote: SharePoint sites can be filtered using the SiteTemplate property during policy configuration.

claims.claim: The notice adds summaries of sensitive information types detected when labels are applied.
claims.quote: Audit and reporting experiences will provide additional visibility, including summaries of the Sensitive Information Types (SITs) detected when labels are applied.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice describes a new 30-day chart showing the number of files processed each day.
claims.quote: A new 30-day processing chart will display the number of files processed each day, helping administrators monitor policy throughput and activity over time.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The enhancements are on by default.
claims.quote: These enhancements are on by default

claims.claim: The enhancements arrive automatically as rollout reaches the organisation.
claims.quote: will be available automatically as the rollout reaches your organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing auto-labeling policies continue functioning without modification.
claims.quote: Existing auto-labeling policies will continue to function without modification.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: action
claims.claim: Microsoft says no action is required.
claims.quote: No action is required.

claims.claim: Microsoft expects no impact on end users.
claims.quote: There is no expected impact to end users.

claims.claim: The notice gives public preview beginning early September 2026 and expected to complete by mid-September 2026.
claims.quote: Public Preview: Available beginning early September 2026 and expected to complete by mid-September 2026.

claims.claim: The notice gives worldwide general availability beginning and expected to complete in mid-November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously late October) and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October).

claims.claim: The 3 November 2026 notice update moved general availability from late October to mid-November.
claims.quote: Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. ... mid-November 2026 (previously late October)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice says the change expands processing capacity rather than changing labeling behaviour.
claims.quote: The change expands processing capacity rather than changing labeling behavior.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn documents simulation support for up to 20,000,000 matched files.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files.

claims.claim: A policy matching more than 20,000,000 files cannot be turned on until it is narrowed and simulation rerun.
claims.quote: If more than this number of files are matched from an auto-labeling policy, you can't turn on the policy to apply the labels. In this case, you must reconfigure the auto-labeling policy so that fewer files are matched, and rerun simulation.

claims.claim: The 20,000,000 matched-file maximum applies only to simulation, not an already enabled policy.
claims.quote: This maximum of 20,000,000 matched files applies to simulation mode only and not to an auto-labeling policy that's already turned on to apply sensitivity labels.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: In the portal, a policy can explicitly include or exclude up to 1,000 SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites

claims.claim: For auto-labeling policies, a SharePoint adaptive scope supports up to 50,000 sites per policy.
claims.quote: For auto-labeling policies, a SharePoint adaptive scope supports up to 50,000 sites per policy.

claims.claim: Learn describes a Labeling activity overview chart with separate successful and failed series covering the last 30 days.
claims.quote: The Overview tab shows labeled and failed file counts and Top 15 sites. Its Labeling activity overview chart has separate successful and failed series for the last 30 days.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning a policy on after simulation requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Review pages require Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Information Protection Admin or Information Protection Analyst.
claims.quote:
To view the review pages, you need one of the following roles:

- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Information Protection Admin
- Information Protection Analyst

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Policies using administrative units must use All for SharePoint and cannot use Included or Excluded.
claims.quote:
For organizations that are using administrative units and selected in the policy:

- For SharePoint, you can't use the Included or Excluded options and must use the All default selection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling applies labels without the user interacting with the process.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: The aggregate tenant-wide maximum is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per day, not a guaranteed rate.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies. This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 auditing must be turned on for simulation.
claims.quote: Auditing is turned on for Microsoft 365. Required for simulation.

claims.claim: Create an auto-labeling policy in Microsoft Purview portal under Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select + Create auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation $spoLocations -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications to add sites.
claims.quote: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation $spoLocations -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes are under Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Name <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -SharePointAdaptiveScopes <AdaptiveScope> -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications.
claims.quote: associate an existing SharePoint adaptive scope with the policy by using the -SharePointAdaptiveScopes parameter (or -SharePointAdaptiveScopesException for exclusions) with New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy.

claims.claim: The Scope Manager role permits creating adaptive scopes and is included in the Compliance Administrator role group.
claims.quote:
Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope. The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups:

- Compliance Administrator

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: An adaptive scope can filter SharePoint site types using SiteTemplate.
claims.quote: an adaptive scope can use the SiteTemplate property to include or exclude communication sites, group-connected sites, Teams private channel sites, classic team sites, or OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Associating an adaptive scope by PowerShell replaces static enumeration with dynamic membership without increasing the portal limit.
claims.quote: This doesn't increase the portal limit; instead, it replaces static site enumeration with dynamic adaptive-scope membership.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Open review pages through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy, then select View details in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: Learn describes Overview, Labeled items and Labeling failures tabs in the newer review page.
claims.quote: The newer review page has separate Overview, Labeled items, and Labeling failures tabs.

claims.claim: The policy details panel has an Insights tab summarising sensitive information types detected in labeled files.
claims.quote: The policy details panel's Insights tab summarizes the sensitive information types detected in labeled files.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Review each policy's details panel, including Insights, for both the SIT summaries and the 30-day chart.
claims.quote: For the daily trend, select View details and open Overview in the newer full review experience. ... This chart isn't part of the newer Insights layout.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'For an enabled policy targeting SharePoint or OneDrive, review the policy details panel's Insights tab for SIT summaries. For the 30-day Labeling activity overview chart, select View details and open Overview in the newer full review experience.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/auto-label-insights-tab.

claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance, Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone) ... Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) ... Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above

claims.claim: The licensing model is included in the named underlying auto-labeling licences, with Learn pointing to the per-SKU guidance.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Separate licensing for these enhancements, including the new reports, has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-labeling" "reporting" "license" "Insights". Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, auto-label-insights-tab and purview-billing-models; no separate enhancement/report licence found.

claims.claim: No separate meter is published for these enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling new SIT reporting Insights licensing additional license pay as you go meter. Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-billing-models and apply-sensitivity-label-automatically; no meter for these auto-labeling enhancements found.

claims.claim: The notice does not mention a charge.
claims.quote: No action is required. ... Review existing auto-labeling policies that were previously constrained by simulation or scope limits.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling is not available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible in the Purview portal when a tenant cannot support the functionality.
claims.quote: If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Learn advises preserving needed results before editing or rerunning simulation.
claims.quote: Before you edit an auto-labeling policy or run simulation again, export any available results that you need for later comparison.

claims.claim: No new role is described for these enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling reporting Insights enable disable tenant switch permissions new role. Opened apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and auto-label-insights-tab; no enhancement-specific new role found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a separate tenant switch for the new reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-labeling" "reporting" "disable" "tenant". Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and auto-label-insights-tab; no separate reporting tenant switch found.

claims.claim: The table lists general auto-labeling targeting controls, not switches for the enhancement rollout.
claims.quote: For the SharePoint location, you can explicitly select up to 1,000 individual sites. To dynamically target sites, use a SharePoint adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating reporting and operational processes to use the new reporting details and throughput metrics.
claims.quote: Update reporting and operational processes to leverage the new Sensitive Information Type reporting details and processing throughput metrics.

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Confirm that the roles you need are assigned ... Confirm auditing is on for Microsoft 365 ... Review each policy's details panel ... Table: explicit SharePoint selection; dynamic SharePoint targeting.
claims.fix: The role-assignment check, auditing check and reporting-review step have no corresponding controls-table rows. Keep this as a coverage note; do not add rows as part of this correction.
